 Order

1. This petition is filed with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.12369/2015 pending before the Court of XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru arising out of Crime No.785/2014 registered by JP Nagar Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC.

entities.text: XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2/de-facto complainant jointly submit that the dispute between the parties, who are husband and wife has been settled.

They have filed an application under Section 320(2) read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking permission of this Court to compound the offences and the said application is supported by Joint Affidavit of the parties.
They accordingly pray to allow the petition.
Parties who are present before the Court are identified by their respective Advocates.

In the Joint Affidavit that is filed in support of the application under Section 320(2) read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C., in paragraph Nos.1 to 4 it has been averred as follows:-
"1.
We submit that both of us are husband and wife and our marriage was solemnized on 25-11-1999 at Srinivasa Kalyana mantapa, Jaraganahalli,.
Both of us have agreed for compromise for the offences punishable under sections 498(A), 504, 506, 323 IPC.

sentences.text:
We humbly submit that petitioner and 2nd respondent have mutually agreed for r e s i d i n g s e p a r a t e l y a s p e r t h e s e t t l e m e n t d a t e d 1 9 / 1 2 / 2 0 2 3 i n CRL.Misc.No.830/2019 and In Crl.Misc.No.881/2018 before the Ist Additional Principal Family Court Judge at Bengaluru, I respectfully submit that both of them are agreed for the same.
3. We submit that the marriage between petitioner and the respondent are completely broken and there is no possibility of reunion.

entities.text: Ist Additional Principal Family Court Judge at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: We are living separately since from 2014.
No meaningful purpose will be NC: 2024:KHC:10290 served in the continuations of legal tie as husband and wife.
We have two major sons.

I have agreed to take Rs.47,00,000/-
(Rupees forty Seven Lakhs Only) as permanent alimony to me By way of Cash and D.D. On date of settlement.
4. We submit that there are no chances of reunion and no chances of leading the happy marital life in future.

Hence both of us agreed to settle the matter as per the settlement taken before the family court."
5.

Respondent No.2/de-facto complainant, who is present in person before the Court acknowledges receipt of Rs.47 lakhs from the petitioner towards permanent alimony as per the terms of the settlement indicated in the Joint Affidavit.

6. Considering the fact that the dispute is between the husband and wife and the alleged offences are compoundable in nature, I am of the opinion that the prayer made in the application filed under Section 320 (2) read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and also in the petition, requires to be allowed.

Accordingly, the following order:-
NC: 2024:KHC:10290 7. I.A.No.1/2024 filed by the parties seeking permission of this Court to compound the offences is allowed.
Parties are permitted to compound the offences for which charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner.

Consequently, the entire proceedings in C.C.No.12369/2015 pending before the Court of XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru arising out of Crime No.785/2014 registered by JP Nagar Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC is quashed.

SD/-
